﻿function Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that signed in recently and are marked compliant, for the devices-compliant measure.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The reader of the devices-compliant measure (powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1), which decides the step
    intune.devices-compliant of the defender's path. A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device
    blocks every device that Microsoft Entra ID doesn't mark compliant, so the share of compliant devices among the
    devices in use says whether such a policy can be turned on.

    Reads the enabled devices in Microsoft Entra ID that signed in within the last SignedInWithinDays days
    (approximateLastSignInDateTime), through the Graph cache. A device counts when isCompliant is true: Intune or
    an approved MDM sets it, and it is what a compliant-device grant checks. Devices that are not compliant are
    returned as the objects that fall short, most recent sign-in first, whether they are managed (isManaged) and
    noncompliant or not managed at all.

    A device that has no Microsoft Entra identity (neither registered nor joined) can't be seen this way, so it is
    neither counted nor listed. A compliant-device policy blocks it too.

    Returns an object with Count (compliant devices), Total (devices that signed in) and Objects (the devices that
    aren't compliant, as Type, Id and DisplayName).

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare

    Returns the number of compliant devices among the enabled devices that signed in within the last 30 days.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare -SignedInWithinDays 14

    Counts only the devices that signed in within the last 14 days.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # Devices that signed in within this many days are counted. approximateLastSignInDateTime is approximate, so
        # keep it well above a week.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $SignedInWithinDays = 30
    )

    # Start of the UTC day, so the request, and so its cache entry, stays the same for the whole day.
    $since = [datetime]::UtcNow.Date.AddDays(-$SignedInWithinDays).ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ', [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture)
    $deviceSplat = @{
        RelativeUri     = 'devices'
        Filter          = "accountEnabled eq true and approximateLastSignInDateTime ge $since"
        # isManaged, operatingSystem and trustType are read for the object facts device.managed, device.os and
        # device.joinType (design section 12), which this reader writes once Add-MtAffectedObjectFact takes a Key.
        Select          = 'id', 'displayName', 'approximateLastSignInDateTime', 'isCompliant', 'isManaged', 'operatingSystem', 'trustType'
        QueryParameters = @{ '$count' = 'true' }
    }
    $devices = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest @deviceSplat | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })

    $notCompliant = @($devices | Where-Object { $_.isCompliant -ne $true })

    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
        Count   = $devices.Count - $notCompliant.Count
        Total   = $devices.Count
        Objects = @(
            $notCompliant |
                Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { $_.approximateLastSignInDateTime -as [datetime] }; Descending = $true }, displayName, id |
                ForEach-Object {
                    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
                        Type        = 'Device'
                        Id          = [string]$_.id
                        DisplayName = [string]$_.displayName
                    }
                }
        )
    }
}
﻿function Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the enabled member users who are registered for multifactor authentication, for the mfa-registered
    measure.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The reader of the mfa-registered measure (powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1), which decides the step
    entra.mfa-registered of the defender's path. User-risk and sign-in-risk policies ask users to complete MFA, and
    a user who hasn't registered a method can't, so the share of registered users says whether those policies can
    be turned on.

    Reads the authentication methods registration report (reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails),
    which needs Microsoft Entra ID P1, through the Graph cache. A member user counts when isMfaRegistered is true.
    Left out of the count:

    - disabled users, which the report also lists;
    - the emergency access accounts in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts), and the users in the
      emergency access groups it names, because they stay excluded from these policies;
    - the users that hold a directory synchronization role, which Conditional Access policies exclude too.

    A configured emergency access account that can't be found stops the reader with an error, as it does in the
    checks that read them, so the figure never counts an account that should have been left out.

    Returns an object with Count (registered users), Total (the users counted) and Objects (the users who aren't
    registered, as Type, Id and DisplayName, administrators first).

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare

    Returns the number of enabled member users who are registered for MFA, apart from the emergency access and
    directory synchronization accounts.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    # The whole report, with no $select or $filter, so other readers of the report share its cache entry.
    $registrations = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails' | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })

    $excluded = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    foreach ($user in @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -Filter 'accountEnabled eq false' -Select 'id' | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })) {
        $null = $excluded.Add([string]$user.id)
    }
    foreach ($account in @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount)) {
        if ($account.Type -eq 'group') {
            $groupUsers = @(Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $account.ObjectId -Recursive | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' })
            foreach ($member in $groupUsers) { $null = $excluded.Add([string]$member.id) }
        } elseif ($account.ObjectId) {
            $null = $excluded.Add([string]$account.ObjectId)
        }
    }
    foreach ($member in @(Get-MtRoleMember -Role 'DirectorySynchronizationAccounts', 'OnPremisesDirectorySyncAccount' | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -ne '#microsoft.graph.servicePrincipal' })) {
        if ($member.id) { $null = $excluded.Add([string]$member.id) }
    }

    $users = @($registrations | Where-Object { $_.userType -eq 'member' -and $_.id -and -not $excluded.Contains([string]$_.id) })
    $notRegistered = @($users | Where-Object { $_.isMfaRegistered -ne $true })

    # The object facts user.mfaRegistered (design section 12), under the object ID and the UPN, are written for
    # these users once Add-MtAffectedObjectFact takes a Key.
    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
        Count   = $users.Count - $notRegistered.Count
        Total   = $users.Count
        Objects = @(
            $notRegistered |
                Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { $_.isAdmin -eq $true }; Descending = $true }, userPrincipalName, id |
                ForEach-Object {
                    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
                        Type        = 'User'
                        Id          = [string]$_.id
                        DisplayName = if ($_.userDisplayName) { [string]$_.userDisplayName } else { [string]$_.userPrincipalName }
                    }
                }
        )
    }
}

function Add-MtAffectedObjectFact {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Adds facts about an object, such as its last sign-in or its expired secrets, to the Affected objects page.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack that knows more about an object than the checks that name
    it: when the object was last used, which permissions it holds, whether its credentials have expired. The facts
    are shown with the object on the Affected objects page of the HTML report and kept in the AffectedObjects of the
    results, the JSON output and the objects files.

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -GraphObjects says which objects a result is about, and adds them to the page with the check
    that named them. Add-MtAffectedObjectFact says what is known about an object, whichever check named it.

    Facts only describe an object that the run already lists. They are merged into the record with the same System,
    Type and Id when the results are built, so adding facts about an object that no check names adds nothing to the
    report. Facts are collected only while Invoke-Maester collects affected objects; otherwise the call does nothing.

    Each fact has a Name, a Value and a Tone: Risk for something to fix, Warning for something to review, Good for a
    sign that the object is in order, and Info (the default) for anything else.

    A fact can also carry a Key and a Raw value, for code that reads the results: a summary, an insight or another
    report. The Key names what the fact is about, from the shared list of fact keys (user.mfaRegistered,
    signIn.daysSince, device.managed...), so the same fact from two sources means the same thing. Raw is its value as
    data: a boolean, a number, a string, a list of strings or a date, which is kept as an ISO 8601 UTC string. Value
    stays the text people read. Raw is kept only with a Key. A fact without a Key is shown the same way.

    Adding a fact with the same Key, or without a Key the same Name, from the same Source again replaces the earlier one.

    The value is shown as text. Name counts rather than other people where you can: the page shows facts to everyone
    who reads the report, and -RedactUserIdentity replaces only the names of users the run knows.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Type ServicePrincipal -Id $sp.id -Source 'Contoso inventory' -Fact @(
        @{ Name = 'Last sign-in'; Value = '2026-06-15 (143 days ago)'; Tone = 'Risk' }
        @{ Name = 'Publisher'; Value = 'Third party (Contoso Ltd)' }
    )

    Adds two facts to an enterprise application.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Type User -Id $user.id -Source 'Contoso HR' -Fact @(
        @{ Name = 'MFA'; Value = 'Not registered'; Tone = 'Risk'; Key = 'user.mfaRegistered'; Raw = $false }
        @{ Name = 'Last sign-in'; Value = '2026-06-15 (143 days ago)'; Tone = 'Warning'; Key = 'signIn.daysSince'; Raw = 143 }
    )

    Adds facts with keys, so code can read whether the user has MFA and how long since they signed in without
    parsing the text.

    .EXAMPLE
    $records | Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Source 'Zero Trust Assessment' -AsOf $report.ExecutedAt

    Adds facts to many objects at once. Each record has Type, Id and Fact properties, and optionally System.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtAffectedObjectFact

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results#adding-facts-about-an-object

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results#fact-keys
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The object type, as the Affected objects page records it: User, Group, ServicePrincipal, AppRegistration
        # (keyed by its appId), Device, ConditionalAccessPolicy, AgentIdentity, AgentIdentityBlueprint, ConfigurationPolicy...
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Type,

        # The object's id, the same id the record uses (for an app registration, its appId).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Id,

        # The facts: hashtables or objects with Name, Value, and optionally Tone (Risk, Warning, Good or Info), Key (a
        # shared fact key such as user.mfaRegistered) and Raw (its value as data).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]

result.output:
## 11. Measures

17 of the 43 steps in the first catalogue have no Maester check (section 15). Two of them are tenant states that
a figure from Graph settles, so in Phase 1 they get measures, not tests. The owner ruled on 5 November 2026 that
readiness is a data point, not a test. A share of compliant devices isn't a misconfiguration and has no meaningful
severity or ATT&CK technique, so it must not change pass rates or the test count. A measure also runs whenever its
step is in scope, so "Before you fix this" shows a real figure even after a one-test run, where a test would have
had to be selected.

A measure is an entry in the measure registry, `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`:

```powershell
@{
    Measures = @(
        @{
            Key         = 'devices-compliant'
            Function    = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
            Title       = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
            Unit        = 'devices'
            Service     = 'Graph'
            License     = 'INTUNE_A'
            Permission  = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All'
        }
    )
}
```

- `Service`, `License` and `Permission` use the grammar of the test attributes, and the engine applies them the
  way it gates a test. A measure whose gate fails is Unknown with the matching reason code.
- `Function` names an internal reader in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`. It reads through the Graph
  cache and returns `Count` (the objects that meet the bar), `Total`, and `Objects` (those that fall short, as
  `Type`, `Id` and `DisplayName`). The engine keeps up to 100 of them.
- The engine works out `Share`, compares it with the step's `MinimumShare` or the run config's override, and
  writes the result to the step (section 7.2).
- Readers write object facts with the shared keys (section 12) for the objects they list.

| Key | Step | Reads | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Entra `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | The objects are the devices a compliant-device policy would block. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so |
| `mfa-registered` | `entra.mfa-registered` | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` for enabled member users | Needs Entra ID P1. Leaves out the emergency access accounts |

Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
see the devices that have no identity yet. The emergency access accounts holding Global Administrator as a
permanent active assignment is another state with no Maester check.

The Defender–Intune connector is not covered. MT.1098 checks the health of the Mobile Threat Defense connectors it
finds, and skips or passes when the Defender connector is missing. The `defender-device-risk` goal needs four
checks before Maester can follow it: the Defender connector is enabled, its compliance toggle is on for each
platform that has a compliance policy, and Windows and Android Enterprise compliance policies require a machine
risk score.

A measure isn't a test: it has no ID, no row in `Tests` and no attribute review, and it plays no part in pass
rates, frameworks or the test count. Packs can't add measures in Phase 1.

## 12. Object facts
## 16. Delivery

| Milestone | Work | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 Format | Schema and loader (`Get-MtStepCatalog`, internal), the `Step` attribute in C#, the schema table and the reader, `StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`, and the compliant-devices goal as the fixture | This design |
| M2 Catalogue | Expert pass on the seven goals against the mirrors, then `Step` on about 75 tests, plus `Step` in the Zero Trust `taxonomy.json` | M1, and the instance-attribute change on `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping` |
| M3 Engine | `Step` on rows, reading the measures of the steps in scope, `Get-MtResultStep` (status, readiness, rank, scope), `LastKnown`, `-Step`, `-IncludePrerequisites`, `Get-MtTest -Step`, CSV and Markdown columns, the console line | M1 |
| M4 Report | Action plan groups and lanes, Before you fix this, rollout in How to fix, the overview card | M3's result shape. It can start on sample data once section 7 is final |
| M5 Measures | The measure registry, the two readers of section 11, and `Measure` on their steps | M1 for the format. The readers can be written before it |
| M6 Tooling | `build/steps/` scripts and the weekly workflow | M1 |
| M7 Docs and site | `Step` in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`, a defender's path page, and one page per goal on maester.dev built by `prepare-data.mjs` | M2 |

Once M1 lands, M2, M5 and M6 touch different files and can run in parallel sessions. M3 and M4 follow in order.

## 17. Decisions

The owner accepted the recommended answer to each decision on 5 November 2026, and changed decision 10 later that day.

# Step catalogue tooling

These scripts keep the defender's path catalogue (`powershell/assets/steps`) in line with Microsoft Learn. The
design is in `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md`, section 13. They read nine public mirrors of Learn that
[merill/learn-mirror](https://github.com/merill/learn-mirror) keeps in git: `merill/entra-docs-mirror`,
`intune-docs-mirror`, `defender-docs-mirror`, `security-docs-mirror`, `purview-docs-mirror`, `teams-docs-mirror`,
`sharepoint-docs-mirror`, `exchange-docs-mirror` and `windows-server-docs-mirror`.

None of them writes to the catalogue. A maintainer reads what they find and edits the catalogue by hand, in
Maester's own words.

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` | Clones or updates the mirrors into `build/steps/.cache` (ignored by git) and writes the URL-to-file index. Asks Learn where each linked URL that no mirror has under that key now goes, and caches the answers for 30 days |
| `Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1` | Pulls the prerequisite sections and the sentences about order from every page that a check guide or a step source links, with the mirror file and line, into `step-candidates.json` for review. `-SuggestNote` also asks a model for Note text, off by default |
| `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` | Lists the step sources whose page changed since its `Reviewed` date. Exits 1 when any needs review |

The functions they share are in `helpers/`, one per file.

## Running them

```powershell
./build/steps/Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1          # about 3 minutes the first time, then seconds
./build/steps/Test-MtStepSource.ps1             # which sources changed since they were reviewed
./build/steps/Test-MtStepSource.ps1 -Step 'entra.*' -ShowDiff
./build/steps/Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1 -Links Catalog
```

The scripts need PowerShell 7.4 or later and git. Only `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` goes to the network (GitHub
for the mirrors, Learn for redirects); the others read the cache. In the blobless clones git fetches an older
version of a page when `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` compares one.

## The weekly issue

`.github/workflows/step-sources.yaml` runs `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` every Monday and on demand. While any source
needs review, one issue labelled `step-sources` stays open, and each run rewrites its list. For each source it
lists:

- **Changed**: the page's text changed since `Reviewed`. Read the diff, update the step if Learn changed what
  comes first, and set `Reviewed` to the date you read it.
- **New**: the page's file is newer than `Reviewed` (the page moved or was published since). Re-read it.
- **NoBaseline**: the mirror starts after `Reviewed`, so it can't show what changed. Re-read the page.
- **NotFound**: no mirror has the page any more. Find where Learn moved it, or another source.
- A redirect or a wrong `Mirror`: cite the URL Learn now uses, or the mirror that holds the page.

When every source is current, the run closes the issue. It never opens pull requests.

## How a change is detected

- `Reviewed` covers the whole day in UTC: the baseline is the mirror's last commit on or before 23:59:59 that day.
- Only the page's body counts. The mirrors commit once per crawl, and a crawl after Learn changes its metadata
  rewrites the front matter of thousands of pages. A commit that changes only front matter is not a change.
- The diff link names the file's anchor on GitHub's commit page. A compare page over a large crawl can be too big
  for GitHub to show one file, so each commit is linked as well, with the file's history.

## Redirects

Check guides link many pages by an old URL (`mem/intune/...`, `microsoft-365/security/...`,
`azure/active-directory/...`). Learn answers a HEAD request for those from a cache that often leaves the redirect
out, so `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` sends a GET that reads only the headers, asks for Markdown as learn-mirror does,
and follows the redirect one hop at a time. Answers are kept in `.cache/redirects.json`. The update also lists the
linked pages that Learn answers 404 for, which are broken links in the check guides.

Draft for Maester 3.1. Main is in the 3.0 code freeze, so this waits until after the release.

## What this is

The defender's path puts fixes in the order that Microsoft Learn documents. It shows what has to be in place before a fix works, what each fix unlocks, and whether the tenant is ready for it. Attack-path tools show the route an attacker takes, but none of them show the order a defender has to work in.

The design is in [`docs/proposals/defenders-path.md`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/feat/defenders-path/docs/proposals/defenders-path.md). All 15 decisions in section 17 were accepted on 5 November 2026. Decision 10 changed later that day: readiness is a measure on a step, not a test.

This PR holds four of the seven milestones. None of it shows up in results or the report yet: `Step` on rows, `Steps`, `Goals`, running the measures, the selectors and the report views come in milestones 3 and 4.

### M1: the format and the attribute

- `Step` on `[MaesterTest]`: the C# class, the schema table and the reader. Values are stored in lowercase, with at most three per test. The engine DLL is rebuilt, and `Build-MaesterEngine.ps1 -Verify` passes.
- `powershell/assets/steps/` holds a JSON schema, `goals.json` and one file per product.
- `Get-MtStepCatalog` (internal) reads and checks the catalogue and orders each goal's steps, prerequisites first.
- `Get-MtStepProblem` (internal) reports catalogue errors, steps the catalogue doesn't have, and measure keys the registry doesn't have. The module build fails on these problems, while a run only warns.
- A shim must declare the same `Step` as the test it calls (`TestShims.Tests.ps1`).

### M2: the first catalogue

- **Size.** 43 steps (27 Entra, 9 Intune, 7 Defender) in eight goals, with 76 sources. Every source is a Learn page described in Maester's own words.
- **Checked against Learn.** Every step and relationship was checked against the Learn mirrors on 5 November. Where Learn disagreed with the draft, Learn won. Section 15 of the design lists each change under "Changes from the draft".
- **The goals:** compliant devices, managed devices, risk policies, phishing-resistant MFA, privileged access, token protection, email authentication, and Defender device risk in compliance.
- **Tests that name a step.** 43 tests, of which 37 are hand-written, 3 are EIDSCA and 3 are ORCA. The EIDSCA and ORCA generators now read `Step` from their metadata files, and the generated tests were regenerated, not edited by hand.
- **Steps with no test.** 17 steps have no Maester test. Two of them get measures (M5). The other 15 say why in `Unchecked`, and for 9 of those the Zero Trust Assessment pack has a check today.
- **Related tests that name no step.** Some tests check a related setting but name no step, because they fail a tenant set up the way Learn describes. Section 15 has a table of them with the reason for each.

### M5: measures

A measure is a figure read from Graph that decides whether a step that describes the state of the tenant is done. It has no test ID and doesn't affect pass rates or the test count.

- `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1` is the registry. Each entry has `Key`, `Function`, `Title`, `Unit`, an optional `Caveat`, `Service`, `License` and `Permission`. `Get-MtMeasureRegistry` (internal) checks every entry.
- A step names its measure as `"Measure": { "Key": "...", "MinimumShare": 95 }`.

| Measure | Step | Reads | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Enabled Entra devices that signed in within 30 days, counted by `isCompliant` | `INTUNE_A`: only Intune marks devices compliant, and a compliance partner's devices need Intune licences too |
| `mfa-capable` | `entra.mfa-registered` | The registration report for enabled member users, counted by `isMfaCapable`, without guests and the emergency access and sync accounts | `AAD_PREMIUM` |

The readers are `Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare` and `Get-MtMfaCapableShare` in `powershell/internal/services/entra/`. Each returns `Count`, `Total` and the objects that fall short, and reads through the Graph cache.

### M6: keeping the catalogue current

`build/steps/` holds three scripts that read the nine public Learn mirrors. None of them writes to the catalogue.

- `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` clones the mirrors into a cache and follows old URLs through Learn's redirects.
- `Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1` pulls the prerequisite sections and the sentences about order from the pages that check guides and step sources link, for a maintainer to review.
- `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` lists the sources whose page changed since their `Reviewed` date.

`.github/workflows/step-sources.yaml` runs `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` every Monday. While any source needs review, it keeps one issue open, and it closes the issue when every source is current. It never opens pull requests.

## Notes for review

- **Which tests name a step.** A test names a step only when a tenant set up the way Learn describes passes it. For example, MT.1013 and CIS 5.2.2.6 reject the Require risk remediation grant that Learn now recommends, so they name no step until they accept it.
- **Compliant devices.** A device only needs to be registered in Entra and enrolled in Intune to be marked compliant, not joined. So the readiness step for that goal is "Devices that sign in are compliant".
- **MFA.** The measure counts `isMfaCapable` rather than `isMfaRegistered`, because a method the authentication methods policy no longer allows can't complete MFA.
- **Caveats.** Each measure has a `Caveat` line, shown with its figure, on what it can't count. For example, the device measure can't count devices that aren't registered or joined in Entra.
- **Object facts.** Facts from #2681 attach only to objects the run lists. So the readers write facts only once M3 shows a measure's objects on the Affected objects page, and M3 also adds a `user.mfaCapable` fact key.
- **Coverage rule.** The rule that every step is named by a test or a measure, or says why in `Unchecked`, runs only in the unit tests (`Get-MtStepProblem -Coverage`). The catalog build also runs on fixture folders that hold only some of the tests, so it can't apply the rule.
- **Issue label.** The weekly workflow creates its `step-sources` label itself. The label isn't in `.github/labels.json` yet.
- **Out of date with main.** The branch is behind main.

## Tests

- New test files:
  - `powershell/tests/functions/engine/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`: catalogue and registry fixtures.
  - `powershell/tests/general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`: the shipped catalogue, its schema and coverage.
  - `powershell/tests/functions/MeasureReaders.Tests.ps1`: what each reader reads, counts and lists.
  - `powershell/tests/general/StepTooling.Tests.ps1`: the `build/steps/` scripts against fixture mirrors, with no network calls.
- 6,972 tests pass in the full suite, and `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` passes.
- `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` was left out locally. One of its tests fails when the Zero Trust Assessment module is installed, and running it starts a real assessment against the connected tenant.

input.description: M3 defender's path engine
input.prompt:
You are building milestone M3 (the engine) of the "defender's path" feature in the Maester repository (PowerShell module for Microsoft 365 security checks).

## Setup
You are in an isolated git worktree. Base your work on local commit 3c3489712 (branch `feat/defenders-path`, which already contains M1, M2, M5, M6 and a fresh merge of main). First run `git checkout -B claude/defenders-path-m3 3c3489712` and confirm `git log -1` shows 3c3489712. Commit your work on that branch (commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Do not push, open PRs or post anything to GitHub.

Read first: `AGENTS.md` (hard rules), and `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md`, the accepted design. It is the spec. Sections 6 (status, readiness, order), 7 (results: rows, `Steps` and `Goals`, other outputs), 8 (selection), 10 (scoping rules), 11 (measures), 12 (object facts), 14 and 16 (the M3 row) matter most. Decision table in section 17. Where the design is silent, choose the simplest thing consistent with it and record the choice in the design doc.

## What already exists (don't rebuild)
- `Step` on `[MaesterTest]` (C# in `src/Maester.Engine/`, DLL in `powershell/lib/`), schema in `powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1`, read by `powershell/internal/engine/Read-MtNativeTest.ps1`. `Get-MtTest MT.1001` already shows `Step`.
- Catalogue `powershell/assets/steps/*.json` (43 steps, 8 goals), loaded by `Get-MtStepCatalog` (internal, cached; returns Steps dictionary, Goals, Problems, and already orders each goal's steps, prerequisites first). `Get-MtStepProblem` for validation.
- Measure registry `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`, loaded by `Get-MtMeasureRegistry` (Key, Function, Title, Unit, Caveat, Service, License, Permission). Readers `Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare` and `Get-MtMfaCapableShare` in `powershell/internal/services/entra/` return Count, Total, Objects (Type, Id, DisplayName). Two steps carry `"Measure": { "Key", "MinimumShare": 95 }`.
- `Add-MtAffectedObjectFact` (public, from main) with fact Key/Raw; shared fact keys listed in `website/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results.md` under "Fact keys".

## What to build (M3)
1. `Step` on result rows.
2. The result's `Steps` and `Goals` (section 7.2), built by a new internal `Get-MtResultStep` (status Done / Not done / Unknown / Not checked / Not applicable with Investigate counting as Unknown; readiness Ready / Blocked / Unconfirmed with `BlockedBy`; rank using unlock value and the test priority; scope rules of section 10; tests listed from the inventory with `NotRun`/`NotInRun` for tests with no row; `OnlyWhen` conditions `hybrid-identity` and `license:<plan>`). The design says the report's `priority()` logic moves into the engine as `Get-MtTestPriority`; find the current priority logic in `report/src/lib/model.ts` / `report/src/pages/report/ActionPlanPage.tsx` and port it faithfully, but do not change the report (another agent owns `report/`).
3. Measures run after the tests for steps in scope, gated by Service/License/Permission like a test, writing `Steps[].Measure` exactly as section 7.2 shows (Key, Count, Total, Share, MinimumShare, Met, ReadAt, Caveat, ObjectCount, Objects up to 100, ReasonCode). Run config `Measures.Enabled` and `Measures.MinimumShare.<key>` (find where run config is resolved, `Resolve-MtRunConfig`). Reads go through the session cache: never use -DisableCache (a unit test enforces this).
4. Facts: per design sections 11–12, put a measure's objects on the Affected objects page and have the two readers write object facts with shared keys (`device.managed`, `device.compliant`, `device.os`, `device.joinType`; for users add a new `user.mfaCapable` key to the shared list in formatting-test-results.md, under the ID and the UPN). If this turns out much larger than expected, do the minimal correct version and document what's left.
5. `LastKnown` in `Get-MtPreviousResult` and `Earlier` on Not checked steps (section 7.2).
6. Selection: `-Step` and `-IncludePrerequisites` on `Invoke-Maester`, `Get-MtTest -Step` (section 8). Include argument completion if the module has a pattern for it. Public parameter changes need comment-based help updates (unit tests enforce help).
7. CSV and Markdown output columns and the console summary line (section 7.3). The console is a TUI renderer; keep the change small.
8. Result schema version bump 2.1 → 2.2 wherever the result schema/version lives, plus any JSON schema file for results.
9. Update the design doc where you made choices.

## Rules
- Don't hand-edit generated files (`powershell/internal/generated/`, `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*`, `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*`, `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/versioned_docs/`). Don't commit website build data (`website/docs/commands/*` except readme.mdx, test-catalog.json, contributors.json, sponsors.json).
- One function per file, Verb-Noun with approved verbs, internal helpers in `powershell/internal/engine/` etc. per AGENTS.md layout.
- Write unit tests for everything new (Pester, under `powershell/tests/functions/...`), with fixtures; no network or tenant calls.
- NEVER run `powershell/tests/functions/ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1`: it starts a real assessment against the connected tenant. Run tests with `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Include '<pattern>'` while iterating, and at the end the full suite: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Exclude 'ZeroTrustAssessmentPack*' -ThrottleLimit 3` (takes several minutes; run it in the background). Also run `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`. Everything must pass.
- Don't connect to any tenant.

## Report back
Branch and final commit SHA; a precise description of the final `Steps`/`Goals`/`Measure` JSON shape (an example object), any deviations from section 7, public API changes (parameters, exported commands), test counts, and open questions. Keep it under 500 words.

input.description: M4 defender's path report
input.prompt:
You are building milestone M4 (the report) of the "defender's path" feature in the Maester repository. Maester's HTML report is a React app in `report/` that builds the template `powershell/assets/ReportTemplate.html`.

## Setup
You are in an isolated git worktree. Base your work on local commit 3c3489712 (branch `feat/defenders-path`). First run `git checkout -B claude/defenders-path-m4 3c3489712` and confirm `git log -1` shows 3c3489712. Commit on that branch (messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Don't push, open PRs or post to GitHub.

Read first: `AGENTS.md`, `report/README.md`, and `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md`, the accepted design and your spec. Section 9 (Report) is what you build; section 7.2 is the exact JSON shape of `Steps` and `Goals` in the result you read (including `Steps[].Measure` with Key, Count, Total, Share, MinimumShare, Met, ReadAt, Caveat, ObjectCount, Objects, ReasonCode, and `Earlier`); sections 6 and 10 explain statuses, readiness and small runs. Decision 15: the defender's path leads the Action plan page, with today's ranked list below.

Another agent is building the engine (M3) in parallel, so no real result file has `Steps` yet. Build against section 7.2 exactly, and add a sample result with `Steps` and `Goals` to whatever sample/fixture data the report uses for development (find it in `report/`). Keep all shape handling in one typed module so a later shape change is a one-file fix. The report must read `Steps` and `Goals` as written and work out nothing itself; when a result has no `Steps`, every view stays exactly as today.

## Build
- Action plan: the defender's path first: groups (Ready now / Blocked / Check first, or as section 9 names them) and one lane per goal in scope, steps in catalogue order with status, readiness, what blocks them, their tests, and the measure figure with its caveat and the objects that hold it back.
- "Before you fix this" on a test page whose test names a step with unmet prerequisites, including the command section 9 gives (`Invoke-Maester -TestId ... -IncludePrerequisites`) and measures/`Earlier` statuses.
- The step's rollout sentences in the How to fix tab.
- The overview card (Ready now, Blocked and Check first counts, linking to the action plan).
- Small runs (1–3 tests): no lanes, only "Before you fix this".
Follow the existing design system, components and wording conventions of the report (see the existing pages; the 3.0 report redesign). Plain, specific UI text.

## Verify
- `cd report && npm ci && npm run build` must pass, plus any lint/typecheck/test scripts in `report/package.json`.
- Check how the built template gets into `powershell/assets/ReportTemplate.html` (a build script or the report build itself) and regenerate it the supported way; don't hand-edit it.
- Run the report dev server and check the new views render with your sample data, with no console errors, in light and dark mode and at phone width. Use the in-app browser preview tools if you have them (create `.claude/launch.json` only in your worktree if needed and don't commit it); otherwise build and open the file headlessly. Take a screenshot or two and save them in the worktree's `TestResults/` (ignored by git) and give their paths.
- Run the PowerShell unit tests that touch the report template: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Include '*Report*','Golden*'`. NEVER run `powershell/tests/functions/ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` (it starts a real assessment against a tenant). Don't connect to any tenant.

## Report back
Branch and final commit SHA, what you built, the TypeScript type you read `Steps`/`Goals` into, anything in section 7.2 that was ambiguous or that you had to assume, screenshot paths, and build/test results. Under 400 words.

The catalogue is `powershell/assets/steps/*.json` (43 steps, 8 goals in `goals.json`), measures in `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`, upkeep scripts in `build/steps/`.

## Build
1. `Step` in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` (and the attribute rubric/reference pages if attributes are documented there): what a step is, when a test names one (only when a tenant set up the way Learn describes passes it; different definitions of done get different steps), the format `<product>.<name>`, max three, and that a step must exist in the catalogue. Also how to add a step to the catalogue (sources in Maester's own words with a Learn URL with no locale, `Reviewed`, `Unchecked`, `Measure`), and the upkeep scripts.
2. A defender's path page explaining the concept to users: goals, steps, statuses (Done, Not done, Unknown, Not checked, Not applicable), readiness (Ready, Blocked, Unconfirmed), measures, and the selectors `Invoke-Maester -Step` and `-IncludePrerequisites` and `Get-MtTest -Step` (being built in parallel by another agent per design section 8; document them as the design specifies). Put it where it fits in the sidebar.
3. One page per goal on maester.dev, built at build time by `website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs` from the catalogue (steps in order with relationships, sources linked, the tests that verify each step taken from the test catalogue data, and the measure). Follow how prepare-data.mjs already generates data (e.g. the test catalog) and how generated pages/data are ignored by git; generated output must not be committed. Link the goal pages from the defender's path page and, if cheap, show a test's step(s) on its test page.
4. Add the new pages to `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md` only if relevant (probably not). If the docs reference `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` guidance on attributes, add `Step` there too (edit the source under `.github/`, then run `./build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1` to regenerate the `.claude/` copies, and commit both).

Writing style: plain, concrete, short sentences, the site's existing voice. No marketing words.

## Verify
- `cd website && npm ci && npm run build` must pass (it runs prepare-data). Check the new pages render: run the dev server and look at them (use in-app browser preview tools if you have them; create `.claude/launch.json` only locally and don't commit it). Save one or two screenshots in `TestResults/` (ignored by git) and give the paths.
- Run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Include 'AgentFiles*','RepositoryLayout*','LanguageNeutral*','*Website*','*Docs*'` and fix what fails. NEVER run `powershell/tests/functions/ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1`. Don't connect to any tenant.
- `git status` before committing: no generated website data committed.

## Report back
Branch and final commit SHA, the pages added (paths and URLs), how goal pages are generated, screenshot paths, build/test results. Under 300 words.

input.content:
Draft for Maester 3.1. Main is in the 3.0 code freeze, so this waits until after the release.

## What this is

The defender's path puts fixes in the order that Microsoft Learn documents. It shows what has to be in place before a fix works, what each fix unlocks, and whether the tenant is ready for it. Attack-path tools show the route an attacker takes, but none of them show the order a defender has to work in.

The design is in [`docs/proposals/defenders-path.md`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/feat/defenders-path/docs/proposals/defenders-path.md). All 15 decisions in section 17 were accepted on 5 November 2026. Decision 10 changed later that day: readiness is a measure on a step, not a test. Section 7.4 records the choices made while building the engine.

This PR holds all seven milestones.

### M1: the format and the attribute

- `Step` on `[MaesterTest]`: the C# class, the schema table and the reader. Values are stored in lowercase, with at most three per test. The engine DLL is rebuilt, and `Build-MaesterEngine.ps1 -Verify` passes.
- `powershell/assets/steps/` holds a JSON schema, `goals.json` and one file per product.
- `Get-MtStepCatalog` (internal) reads and checks the catalogue and orders each goal's steps, prerequisites first.
- `Get-MtStepProblem` (internal) reports catalogue errors, steps the catalogue doesn't have, and measure keys the registry doesn't have. The module build fails on these problems; a run only warns.
- A shim must declare the same `Step` as the test it calls (`TestShims.Tests.ps1`).

### M2: the first catalogue

- 43 steps (27 Entra, 9 Intune, 7 Defender) in eight goals, with 76 sources. Every source is a Learn page described in Maester's own words.
- Every step and relationship was checked against the Learn mirrors on 5 November. Where Learn disagreed with the draft, Learn won (section 15, "Changes from the draft").
- The goals: compliant devices, managed devices, risk policies, phishing-resistant MFA, privileged access, token protection, email authentication, and Defender device risk in compliance.
- 43 tests name a step: 37 hand-written, 3 EIDSCA and 3 ORCA. The EIDSCA and ORCA generators read `Step` from their metadata files.
- 17 steps have no Maester test. Two get measures (M5); the other 15 say why in `Unchecked`, and for 9 of those the Zero Trust Assessment pack has a check today.
- Tests that check a related setting but fail a tenant set up the way Learn describes name no step. Section 15 lists them with the reason for each.

### M3: the engine

- Result rows carry `Step`. The result has `Steps` and `Goals`, built by `Get-MtResultStep` (internal). Each step has a status (Done, Not done, Unknown, Not checked, Not applicable), readiness (Ready, Unconfirmed, Blocked) with what blocks it, a rank, what it unlocks, its tests from the inventory (with `NotInRun` for tests that didn't run), its measure, and `Earlier` when an earlier run checked it.
- The rank uses the report's priority, now in the engine as `Get-MtTestPriority`.
- Measures run right after the tests for the steps in scope. They're gated by service, licence and permission like a test, and read through the Graph cache. Run config: `Measures.Enabled` and `Measures.MinimumShare.<key>`.
- A measure's objects go on the Affected objects page with source `Measure`. The readers write the device facts and `user.mfaCapable` / `user.mfaRegistered`; `user.mfaCapable` is added to the shared fact keys.
- `Get-MtPreviousResult` gains `LastKnown`.
- Selection: `Invoke-Maester -Step` and `-IncludePrerequisites`, `Get-MtTest -Step`, with tab completion, and `Selection.Step` / `Selection.IncludePrerequisites` in run config.
- The CSV gains `Step`, `Readiness` and `BlockedBy` columns. Partitioned runs rebuild `Steps` and `Goals` from the merged rows.
- `SchemaVersion` is `2.2`, documented in `result-schema.md`.

### M4: the report

- The Action plan leads with the defender's path: step cards grouped as Ready now, Check first and Blocked, in rank order. Each card shows its tests, the measure with its caveat and the objects that fall short, what blocks it, what it unlocks, rollout and sources. Below are one lane per goal and today's ranked list. Failures whose step is blocked move last and say what blocks them.
- Test pages get "Before you fix this", which lists unmet prerequisites with the `-IncludePrerequisites` command. How to fix gains "Roll it out safely".
- The Overview has a card with the three counts. Runs of one to three tests get no lanes and no card.
- A result with no `Steps` looks exactly as before. All shape handling is in `report/src/lib/defendersPath.ts`; sample data is in `sampleSteps.ts` (`?sample=step` for a one-test run).

### M5: measures

| Measure | Step | Reads | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Enabled Entra devices that signed in within 30 days, counted by `isCompliant` | `INTUNE_A`: only Intune marks devices compliant, and a compliance partner's devices need Intune licences too |
| `mfa-capable` | `entra.mfa-registered` | The registration report for enabled member users, counted by `isMfaCapable`, without guests and the emergency access and sync accounts | `AAD_PREMIUM` |

The registry is `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`. A measure has no test ID and doesn't affect pass rates or the test count. Each has a `Caveat` line on what it can't count.

### M6: keeping the catalogue current

`build/steps/` holds `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1`, `Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1` and `Test-MtStepSource.ps1`, which read the nine public Learn mirrors and never write to the catalogue. `.github/workflows/step-sources.yaml` runs every Monday and keeps one issue open while any cited Learn page changed since it was reviewed.

### M7: docs and site

- A defender's path page (`/docs/defenders-path`) and one page per goal (`/docs/defenders-path/<goal>`), generated by `prepare-data.mjs` from the catalogue at build time and ignored by git.
- `Step` in the writing-tests guide, the attribute rubric and the test expert skill. Each test page links its steps.
- Run configuration, result schema and fact key docs for the M3 changes.

## Notes for review

- **Which tests name a step.** Only tests that pass a tenant set up the way Learn describes. For example, MT.1013 and CIS 5.2.2.6 reject the Require risk remediation grant that Learn now recommends, so they name no step until they accept it.
- **Goal lanes after a narrow run.** A goal is in scope when any of its steps is. So `-Step entra.ca-require-compliant-device -IncludePrerequisites` also shows lanes for other goals that share the foundation steps, such as risk policies with three of its steps. This follows the design; it may be worth limiting.
- **New measure reason codes.** `PermissionNotGranted`, `MeasureError` and `MeasureOff` are new, because tests have no permission gate to borrow a code from.
- **Coverage rule.** The rule that every step is named by a test or a measure, or says why in `Unchecked`, runs only in the unit tests (`Get-MtStepProblem -Coverage`), because the catalog build also runs on fixture folders.
- **Issue label.** The weekly workflow creates its `step-sources` label itself. The label isn't in `.github/labels.json` yet.

## Tests

- New test files: `engine/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`, `general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`, `MeasureReaders.Tests.ps1`, `general/StepTooling.Tests.ps1` and `engine/DefendersPath.Tests.ps1`.
- The full suite passed locally on the branch before the latest update from main (7,129 tests, after regenerating `test-builder.json`). After that update, the 1,341 tests in the affected files pass. `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`, `npm run build` in `report/` (the committed template matches it) and `npm run build` in `website/` pass.
- End to end without a tenant: `Invoke-Maester -Step entra.ca-require-compliant-device -IncludePrerequisites -SkipGraphConnect` writes schema 2.2 with eight ranked steps. Their statuses are Unknown with reasons such as `ServiceNotConnected` and `NoCheck`, never Not done. The HTML report shows them on the Action plan with no console errors.
- Not tested against a tenant yet.
- `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` was left out locally. One of its tests fails when the Zero Trust Assessment module is installed, and running it starts a real assessment against the connected tenant.

content.text:
All seven milestones are done, merged into `feat/defenders-path` and pushed to draft PR [maester365/maester#2683](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2683), now titled "feat: the defender's path (M1–M7)". It hasn't been run against a tenant yet, and CI on the latest push hasn't reported.

**What's new since M1, M2, M5 and M6:**
- **M3, engine:**
  - Results now include `Steps` and `Goals`, using schema 2.2. Each step has a status, readiness, what blocks it, a rank and what it unlocks.
  - Measures run for the steps in scope, and their objects and facts go on the Affected objects page.
  - New selectors: `-Step` / `-IncludePrerequisites` on `Invoke-Maester`, and `-Step` on `Get-MtTest`.
  - The CSV gains `Step`, `Readiness` and `BlockedBy` columns.
- **M4, report:**
  - The Action plan opens with step cards grouped as Ready now, Check first and Blocked, followed by goal lanes and today's ranked list.
  - Test pages get "Before you fix this", How to fix gets the rollout, and the Overview gets a count card.
  - A result without `Steps` looks the same as today.
- **M7, docs and site:** a defender's path page and one generated maester.dev page per goal. `Step` is documented in the writing-tests guide, the attribute rubric and the test expert skill.

**How it was checked.** The three agents couldn't run PowerShell in their worktrees, so I ran everything myself:
- **Unit tests:** the full suite passed, 7,129 tests, once I fixed three failures. One test read the array's own `Rank` property instead of each step's rank, two analyzer warnings were false alarms, and the test builder data needed regenerating.
- **Builds:** the module, report and website builds pass, and the report template in the repo matches a fresh build.
- **Offline end-to-end run:** `Invoke-Maester -Step entra.ca-require-compliant-device -IncludePrerequisites -SkipGraphConnect` wrote eight ranked steps. Their statuses are Unknown with a reason, never Not done. The HTML report showed them on the Action plan with no console errors.
- **After the update from main:** someone merged main into the branch on GitHub while this was running. I merged that in, reran the 1,341 tests in the affected files (all pass), and left the full suite to CI.

**Worth a look when you review:**
- **Lanes from a narrow run:** a run scoped to one goal also shows lanes for other goals that share its foundation steps, such as risk policies with three steps. That follows the design's "a goal is in scope when any of its steps is", but it's noisy and may be worth limiting.
- **Missing label:** the weekly workflow's `step-sources` label still isn't in `.github/labels.json`.

To try it against your tenant, run `Invoke-Maester -Step entra.ca-require-compliant-device -IncludePrerequisites` from the worktree and open the Action plan.

okay I reviewed the sample report and I'm not super impressed with the output. I don't think all of the changes we made in design is worth the output produced by the report now..

I think you're right about the report. I opened the end-to-end report myself, and it shows the problem.

**The report shows the machinery, not the answer.** The Action plan opened with "0 steps ready now, 0 blocked" and eight "Check first" cards. Each card said, in its own words, "this run could not tell". Each card carries a status, readiness, rank, unlocks, tests, a measure, sources and rollout. Every field is correct, but together they read like a database record, not advice. The one sentence a defender needs ("fix these two things before you turn on that policy") is buried in it.

**Most real tenants won't look much better.**
- 15 of the 43 steps have no Maester check.
- 9 more steps are checked only by the Zero Trust pack, which can't report steps yet.
- Measures need permissions many people won't grant.

So a lot of a real run will be "Not checked" or "Unknown". The design is careful never to call those Not done, which is right, but it means the screen fills with hedges.

**The cost is out of proportion.** The data layer (the catalogue, `Step` on tests, the two measures) is small and is the part nobody else has. Most of the weight is in the report and engine on top of it: five statuses, three readiness states, ranking, goal lanes, cards, `Earlier`, and schema 2.2. That's what isn't paying off.

What I'd keep and what I'd cut:

1. **Keep** the catalogue, `Step` and the measures. They're cheap, checked against Learn, and other things can build on them.
2. **Cut the report down to two things:**
   - On a failing test, a short "Do these first" line naming the unmet prerequisites. It shows only when there are some.
   - One ordered checklist per goal, showing only what failed or is missing, in Learn's order.
   No cards, no readiness labels, no rank numbers, no "check first" group.
3. **Simplify the engine output to match.** Also drop the goal lanes from narrow runs, and probably `Earlier`.

The PR is a draft until 3.1, so nothing ships either way. Undoing parts of M3 and M4 is cheap now.

Before I change anything: what put you off most? Was it the look of the cards, the amount of "couldn't tell", or that it didn't say anything you couldn't already see from the failed tests? The answer changes what to cut.

Separately, the CIS.M365.4.1 shim session confirmed that the shim is still only uncommitted edits on `claude/elegant-spence-176024`, in no PR.

result.output:
# Microsoft Zero Trust Framework Explorer

An interactive explorer for Microsoft's [Zero Trust Workshop](https://zerotrust.microsoft.com/). Browse all seven pillars, their functional areas, and tasks that make up the framework — each viewable as an interactive mindmap.

**Live site:** [zerotrustexplorer.merill.net](https://zerotrustexplorer.merill.net)

## What is this?

Microsoft's [Zero Trust Workshop](https://zerotrust.microsoft.com/) is a wealth of knowledge on implementing Zero Trust using the Microsoft Security stack. It's designed to be used when running a series of workshops with a customer, walking through each pillar of the Zero Trust framework.

As a side effect of being a workshop tool, the depth of guidance it contains isn't always in an easily digestible form for someone who simply wants to learn. This site reorganizes that knowledge into an interactive knowledge tree that you can explore at your own pace — spanning identity, devices, data, network, infrastructure, security operations, and AI.

Whether you're a security architect, IT admin, or just curious about how Microsoft approaches Zero Trust, this site aims to make the concepts approachable and the guidance easy to navigate.

## Features

- **Overview dashboard** — Browse all 7 pillars with their functional areas and tasks in a card grid
- **Interactive mindmaps** — Explore each pillar as a zoomable, pannable mindmap
- **Zero Trust Book** — A printable, long-form reference with chapters per pillar and PDF export
- **Auto-synced content** — Data stays current via daily automated sync from upstream sources

## Pillars

| Pillar | Description |
|---|---|
| Identity | Identity and access management |
| Devices | Device compliance and management |
| Data | Data protection and governance |
| Network | Network security and segmentation |
| Infrastructure | Application and infrastructure security |
| Security Operations | Threat detection, investigation, and response |
| AI | AI security posture, agent governance, and threat protection |

## How it's built

The site is a React app (TypeScript + Vite) that pulls its data directly from the upstream Zero Trust Workshop sources. No content is manually copied or maintained here — everything stays in sync automatically.

A daily automated sync runs via GitHub Actions every morning at 6 AM UTC. It fetches the latest pillar data from [zerotrust.microsoft.com](https://zerotrust.microsoft.com/) and pulls the workshop documentation (Markdown) from the [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment) GitHub repository. When changes are detected upstream, they're committed to this repository automatically — keeping the content fresh without any manual intervention.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Who built this?

This is a personal project by [Merill Fernando](https://merill.net), a Product Manager at Microsoft.

name: Sync upstream Zero Trust data

on:
  schedule:
    # Daily at 6:00 AM UTC
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    # Allow manual trigger from GitHub UI

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run sync script
        run: node scripts/sync-upstream.mjs

      - name: Build book data
        run: node scripts/build-book.mjs

      - name: Check for changes
        id: changes
        run: |
          git add -A
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No changes detected"
          else
            echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Changes detected:"
            git diff --cached --stat
          fi

      - name: Commit and push
        if: steps.changes.outputs.changed == 'true'
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit -m "chore: sync upstream Zero Trust data ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))"
          git push

input.ask: Is this view worth building?

content.text:
Yes, we can map our tests onto the mind map. Most of the mapping already exists, and the mockup above shows how it could look.

**What ztexplorer is.** It pulls Microsoft's Zero Trust Workshop data every day. That's 7 pillars and 741 tasks, grouped by functional area and then by swimlane, which is exactly the mind map's tree. Each task already carries what guidance needs:
- a phase (First, Then, Next);
- a priority (P0–P3);
- effort and user impact;
- a licence;
- a CISA maturity stage;
- the tasks it depends on.

Microsoft wrote that order, so we wouldn't need our own catalogue.

**How our tests map onto it.** Two mappings already exist:
- **Zero Trust Assessment checks to tasks:** Microsoft ships `ztw-task-mapping.json` in the zerotrustassessment repo. It's maintained, and ZTA uses it to import results into the workshop.
- **Maester tests to ZTA checks:** our ZTA pack's `taxonomy.json` lists the Maester, CIS, CISA and EIDSCA tests that check the same thing (`AlsoCheckedBy`) for 53 checks. Through those, our own tests land on the same tasks.

Maester runs the ZTA checks through the pack, so a run with the pack covers the most tasks. Without it, only the tasks those 53 links reach would light up.

**How much of the map would light up.**

| Pillar | Tasks | Tasks with at least one check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | 113 | 40 |
| Devices | 142 | 25 |
| Data | 26 | 13 |
| Network | 96 | 41 |
| AI | 92 | 15 |
| Infrastructure | 147 | 0 |
| Security Ops | 125 | 0 |

So about 134 of the 741 tasks can be checked automatically. That's why the mockup counts only checkable tasks ("22 of 40"), shows the rest as dotted "review it yourself" nodes, and says plainly when a pillar has no checks yet.

**What's different from the defender's path.**
- The order and dependencies are Microsoft's, already published and kept current. We'd maintain nothing.
- The mind map is a picture people already know from the workshop and your site. A green, amber or red dot per task reads at a glance.
- Guidance becomes simple: finish the First tasks that are failing, P0 first, then Then. Each item names the failing checks and the objects behind them, and links to the workshop page for that task.

**Things to decide before building:**
- **Where the data lives.** We'd copy ztexplorer's pillar files and Microsoft's mapping into Maester's build, or fetch them at build time like ztexplorer does. They aren't our content, so we'd need to check the licence and attribution.
- **What "done" means for a task.** The mockup's rule is "all mapped checks pass". A task like "Design Conditional Access posture" is mostly planning, and its three checks only cover part of it.
- **What happens to PR 2683.** This view would replace most of it. We'd keep `Step` and the measures only if they still earn their place; the step catalogue becomes unnecessary.

#  Enforce authentication with strong creds for all privileged accounts

**Implementation Effort:** High – Implementing strong authentication methods for all privileged accounts requires coordinated efforts across IT, security, and application teams to audit, assess, and reconfigure authentication mechanisms, often involving multiple systems and stakeholders.

**User Impact:** Low – Administrators must adopt new authentication methods, which may need training and adjustments to their workflows.

## Overview

Enforcing authentication strength  for all privileged accounts is essential to protect sensitive resources. This involves mandating the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, or certificate-based authentication, through Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra ID. By leveraging the authentication strengths feature, organizations can specify required authentication methods for accessing critical resources, ensuring that only verified and authorized users can perform high-privilege operations. This approach aligns with the Zero Trust principles of "Verify explicitly" by continuously validating user identities and "Use least privilege access" by restricting access based on strong authentication. Failure to implement these measures can expose organizations to credential-based attacks, unauthorized access, and potential data breaches.

## Reference

* [Overview of Microsoft Entra authentication strength](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strengths)
* [How Conditional Access authentication strength works](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-how-it-works)
* [Custom Conditional Access authentication strengths](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-strength-advanced-options)
