content.text:
The review reports are ready. Open [scratch/report-variants/index.html](scratch/report-variants/index.html): it links 20 reports, covering 7 scenarios each in wordings A, B and C (the tenant scenario has only A and B). They're also open in the browser pane at http://localhost:8766/index.html.

**Wording suggestions for a run with no tenant**

| | Top bar | Eyebrow | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A, neutral** (my pick) | date only | Maester report | 54% of the checks that ran passed |
| **B, machine** | Merills-MacBook-Pro | Test report, or Security report if any built-in tests ran | This run passed 54% of the checks that ran |
| **C, suite** | PoraLocal | Maester report | PoraLocal passed 54% of the checks that ran |

I recommend A. It never claims what the report is about, and "Maester report" is true whatever tests ran. B can put a machine name into a report someone shares. C depends on the suite ID, which is often something like `Custom`.

**What applies in every wording**

- **Report subject:**
  - The placeholder "TenantName (not connected to Graph)" is gone.
  - A run names its tenant if it connected to one.
  - A run connected only to Active Directory names its domain. In the AD scenario that's "corp.contoso.com passed 57%…".
- **Lead sentence:** it only says "because a service, licence or permission was missing" when that is actually why tests didn't run.
- **Runs with no scored checks:** the title says "No check gave a pass or fail" instead of "passed 0%".
- **Tests with no attributes:** the bare scenario now looks tidy.
  - No fake "Custom" product.
  - The "Critical and high" and "Quick wins" cards are hidden.
  - The "Failed by severity" card is hidden. It used to say "Nothing failed" while 3 tests had failed.
  - The fix list says the tests are listed in run order, because they declare no severity.
- **Failed by severity:** the card hides when nothing failed. A failure with no severity shows as "Not rated".
- **Wording:**
  - "Does not apply" no longer mentions "the tenant".
  - The footer says the report holds data from the subject, or "the systems its tests read".

**Things to know**

- The A/B/C switch (`window.__mtTitleVariant` in `report/src/lib/runSubject.ts`) is temporary. I'll remove the wordings you don't pick.
- PowerShell still writes the placeholder strings into the JSON; the report just ignores them now. Writing `null` there instead would be a small follow-up, but it changes the JSON other tools read.
- Two background servers are running for the browser pane, on ports 8765 and 8766.
- The `graph-connected` scenario uses the run you made against Pora.
- I checked the bare, AD, demo, Graph-offline and tenant scenarios in the pane, with no console errors. Nothing is committed.

content.text:
While the unit tests finish (I'll commit and push once they pass), here are options for mentioning Maester Cloud. I looked for places where the report already shows a limit of a one-off local run, so the mention reads as help rather than an ad. They're ordered from most to least subtle.

**1. Where a single run falls short (my top pick)**
- **Trend card:** with only one run, the pass-rate trend is empty. Add one muted line there: *"See this trend over time: Maester Cloud runs these checks daily and keeps the history."*
- **Changes strip:** on a first run there's no "new failures since…" comparison. Show *"Get told when a result changes"* there.

These only show when the reader has hit that limit, and they disappear once there's history, so a regular user rarely sees them.

**2. Footer credit**
- Today it reads: "Generated by Maester 3.0.0 · maester.dev".
- Extend it to: "… · maester.dev · Run it on a schedule with **maester.cloud**".
- It's on every page, small and below the content. It's the most "standard" place, but it's also the most ignorable.

**3. Run details page**
- That page already explains how the report was made: the command, the machine, the duration.
- Add one row: *"Ran on Merills-MacBook-Pro. Maester Cloud can run it for you, with no machine to keep on."*
- It's a factual comparison in the place people go to learn how runs work.

**4. Action plan**
- People open the action plan to work through fixes.
- Add a note at the bottom: *"Assign these to people and track them to done in Maester Cloud."*
- This aims at the strongest buying moment, a team acting on the findings. It's a step more "salesy".

**5. Tenant switcher, for reports that combine several tenants**
- Add a line under the tenant list: *"Compare every tenant you manage, every day, in Maester Cloud."*
- It only appears in multi-tenant reports, which is your MSP and partner audience.

**6. Export menu**
- Add a last item: "Share with your team" → Maester Cloud. It sits next to the CSV and Markdown exports.
- Make it a link with a "↗", not something that pretends to share the report.

**Guardrails I'd keep for any of them**
- **One mention per page at most:** every option shows only in context, so none of them stack.
- **Plain links only:** no tracking pixel or remote image, so the report stays offline and private. A `?ref=report` on the link is enough for you to count visits.
- **A way to turn them off:** a config switch such as `Report.HideMaesterCloud`, for consultants who hand reports to their clients.
- **Never above the fold:** keep them out of the overview's header and KPI cards.

My suggestion is option 1 plus the footer line (option 2), with option 5 for multi-tenant reports. Tell me which ones you want and I'll build them; nothing for this is in the commit.

The third was the explainer reminder: the "How Maester works" explainer's narration still matches the report, but its screenshots show the old left menu. Updating them means re-recording that explainer, so I left it for now.

The full unit suite didn't run on this commit: the change is two small edits, and the TypeScript build and the analyzer both passed.
